title: DC Motors — Back EMF, Torque & Speed Control
subtitle: DC motors convert electrical energy into mechanical rotation. Back EMF is the self-regulating mechanism. Torque and speed are deeply connected through flux and armature current. These are the most examined topics in ECE 210.
learningOutcome: DC motors convert electrical energy into mechanical rotation. Back EMF is the self-regulating mechanism. Torque and speed are deeply connected through flux and armature current. These are the most examined topics in ECE 210.

topics.title: Back EMF, Torque, Speed & Maximum Power

subtopics.title: Back EMF, Torque, Speed & Maximum Power

content.text: A rotating armature generates back EMF Eb = kNφ opposing supply voltage V. Motor equation: V = Eb + IaRa. At start-up Eb=0 → huge Ia=V/Ra — need starting resistors. As speed builds, Eb rises, Ia falls to normal operating level.
Torque: T = 0.159×Z×φ×P×(Ia/a). So T ∝ φIa. Shunt: φ constant → T ∝ Ia. Series: φ ∝ Ia → T ∝ Ia² (huge starting torque).
Speed: N ∝ Eb/φ = (V−IaRa)/φ. Reduce φ → speed increases (used in speed control).

Maximum power condition: P = Eb×Ia = (V−IaRa)×Ia. Differentiate: dP/dIa = V−2IaRa = 0 → Eb = V/2. Maximum power when back EMF = half supply voltage. (Efficiency only 50% at this point — not the efficient operating point.)

Common mistake — Generator: V = E−IaRa. Motor: V = Eb+IaRa. These are opposite signs — do not swap them. Also: when comparing two operating points, Eb changes at each point (because Ia changed). Always recalculate Eb separately at each operating condition.

Exam-ready — series motor no-load danger:
A series motor must never run on no-load because at no load Ia → 0 → φ → 0. Since N ∝ Eb/φ and φ approaches zero, speed increases without limit — the motor runs away and can reach destructive speeds causing mechanical failure. Series motors must always be permanently coupled to their load.
